lines.rookie:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people walk to the market, like shoppers.
They come because they saw our sign the night before.
Our sign is a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell. A bell is too loud.
lines.junior:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people walk to the market as if they are shoppers.
They come because they saw our sign the night before.
Our sign will be a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell. A bell makes too much noise.
lines.master:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people stroll to the market, as though they were ordinary shoppers.
They come because they spotted our sign the night before.
Our sign shall be a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell: a bell would be far too loud.

lines.junior: Harbin in 1909 and Aunae in 1919: the same water drop. What is inside the old box?
lines.master: Harbin in 1909, Aunae in 1919, and one water drop. What lies inside the old box?

lines.rookie: the night before
lines.junior: the night before
lines.master: the night before

lines.rookie: March has thirty-one days.
lines.junior: March has thirty-one days.
lines.master: March has thirty-one days.

lines.rookie: MAEBONG HILL
lines.junior: MAEBONG HILL
lines.master: MAEBONG HILL

lines.rookie: At dusk, Gyeongsun leads you up Maebong hill.
lines.junior: As the sun sets, Gyeongsun takes you up Maebong hill.
lines.master: At dusk, Gyeongsun guides you up the slope of Maebong hill.

lines.rookie: She carries an old wooden box with a small dial lock.
lines.junior: She is carrying an old wooden box with a little dial lock.
lines.master: In her arms is an old wooden box fitted with a small dial lock.

lines.rookie: "I put Gwan-sun's plan inside. The stranger must not read it."
lines.junior: "I put Gwan-sun's plan in here. The stranger must never read it."
lines.master: "Gwan-sun's plan is inside. The stranger must never lay eyes on it."

lines.rookie: Gyeongsun whispers:
lines.junior: Gyeongsun says quietly:
lines.master: Gyeongsun murmurs:

lines.rookie:
I set the lock to our two days.
First two dials: the night of the sign. It is a night in March.
Last dial: the day of the march, in April.
Remember: March has thirty-one days.
The sign burns the night before the march.
lines.junior:
I set the lock to our two days.
The first two dials: the night of the sign, a night in March.
The last dial: the day of the march, in April.
Don't forget: March has thirty-one days.
The sign burns the night before the march.
lines.master:
The lock is set to our two days.
The first two dials hold the night of the sign, which falls in March.
The last dial holds the day of the march, in April.
Bear in mind: March has thirty-one days.
The sign burns the night before the march.

lines.rookie: Turn the dials to the night of the sign and the day of the march.
lines.junior: Set the dials to the night of the sign and then the day of the march.
lines.master: Turn the dials to the night of the sign, followed by the day of the march.

lines.rookie: Your notes say the day of the march. Your plan says when the sign burns.
lines.junior: Your notes give the day of the march. Your plan tells when the sign burns.
lines.master: Your notes hold the day of the march; the plan reveals when the sign is lit.

lines.rookie: The night before the first of April is the last night of March.
lines.junior: The last night of March is the night before the first of April.
lines.master: The night preceding the first of April is the final night of March.

lines.rookie: The old box opens!
lines.junior: The old box is open!
lines.master: The old box swings open!

lines.rookie: Below, the villages are dark and quiet.
lines.junior: Down below, the villages are dark and silent.
lines.master: Far below, the villages lie dark and silent.

lines.rookie: Then a small flame rises on Maebong hill.
lines.junior: Then a little flame starts to rise on Maebong hill.
lines.master: Then a small flame climbs into the dark on Maebong hill.

lines.rookie: Far away, on other hills, you see more lights.
lines.junior: In the distance, more lights appear on other hills.
lines.master: In the distance, one hilltop after another answers with its own light.

lines.rookie: First the night of the sign, then the day of the march.
lines.junior: The night of the sign comes first, and then the day of the march.
lines.master: The night of the sign must come first, the day of the march after it.

lines.rookie: March has thirty-one days. The night before April 1 is the last night of March.
lines.junior: March has thirty-one days, so the night before April 1 is the last night of March.
lines.master: March has thirty-one days; the night before April 1 is therefore the final night of March.

lines.rookie: The march is on the first of April, not the second.
lines.junior: The march is on the first of April, not on the second.
lines.master: The march falls on the first of April, not the second.

lines.rookie: That is Mr. Pyo's day. Two messengers said the first of April.
lines.junior: That is the day Mr. Pyo gave. Two messengers said the first of April.
lines.master: That is Mr. Pyo's false day. Two messengers agreed on the first of April.

lines.rookie: These numbers fit, but not in this order. The night of the sign comes first.
lines.junior: These numbers are right, but in the wrong order. The night of the sign is first.
lines.master: The numbers are right but misplaced. The night of the sign comes first.

lines.rookie: Under the plan lie old notes, each with a water drop.
lines.junior: Old notes lie under the plan, and each one has a water drop.
lines.master: Beneath the plan lie older notes, each marked with a water drop.

lines.rookie: The oldest is at the bottom. One corner is burnt.
lines.junior: The oldest one is at the very bottom. One of its corners is burnt.
lines.master: The oldest rests at the very bottom, one corner scorched.

lines.rookie: It says 훈민정음. This is Bun-i's note from 1446!
lines.junior: It says 훈민정음. It's Bun-i's note from 1446!
lines.master: It reads 훈민정음. This is Bun-i's very note from 1446!

lines.rookie: Bun-i was our first keeper. We are all her family.
lines.junior: Bun-i was our very first keeper. We are all part of her family.
lines.master: Bun-i was the first of our keepers. Every one of us is her family.

lines.rookie: That night, Gwan-sun lights the fire on Maebong hill.
lines.junior: That night, Gwan-sun lights the fire up on Maebong hill.
lines.master: That night, Gwan-sun sets the fire blazing on Maebong hill.

lines.rookie: On 1 April 1919, thousands of people gather at Aunae Market.
lines.junior: On 1 April 1919, thousands of people come together at Aunae Market.
lines.master: On 1 April 1919, thousands of people gather in Aunae Market.

lines.rookie: Gwan-sun leads them. They call for Korea's independence.
lines.junior: Gwan-sun leads the crowd, and they call for Korea's independence.
lines.master: With Gwan-sun at their head, they call for Korea's independence.
